claim: The Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling pathway controls embryonic development and tissue homeostasis after birth.
source: The Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling pathway controls embryonic development and tissue homeostasis after birth.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, representing general scientific knowledge about Shh function.

claim: Dual-lipidated Shh precursors are firmly plasma membrane-associated.
source: This requires regulated solubilization of dual-lipidated, firmly plasma membrane-associated Shh precursors from producing cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the biochemical properties of lipidated Shh.

claim: The resistance-nodulation-division transporter Dispatched (Disp) drives the solubilization of dual-lipidated Shh from producing cells.
source: Although it is firmly established that the resistance-nodulation-division transporter Dispatched (Disp) drives this process, it is less clear how lipidated Shh solubilization from the plasma membrane is achieved.
evidence: This statement references established findings in the field.

claim: Disp promotes proteolytic solubilization of Shh from its lipidated terminal peptide anchors.
source: We have previously shown that Disp promotes proteolytic solubilization of Shh from its lipidated terminal peptide anchors.
evidence: The authors cite their own previous work.

claim: Shedding converts tightly membrane-associated hydrophobic Shh precursors into delipidated soluble proteins.
source: This process, termed shedding, converts tightly membrane-associated hydrophobic Shh precursors into delipidated soluble proteins.
evidence: This is a definition and characterization of the shedding process based on the authors' previous work.

claim: Disp-mediated Shh shedding is modulated by a serum factor identified as high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
source: We show here that Disp-mediated Shh shedding is modulated by a serum factor that we identify as high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study supported by experimental data.

claim: HDLs serve as a soluble sink for free membrane cholesterol.
source: In addition to serving as a soluble sink for free membrane cholesterol, HDLs also accept the cholesterol-modified Shh peptide from Disp.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HDL function in cholesterol metabolism.

claim: HDLs accept the cholesterol-modified Shh peptide from Disp.
source: In addition to serving as a soluble sink for free membrane cholesterol, HDLs also accept the cholesterol-modified Shh peptide from Disp.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study supported by experimental data.

claim: The cholesteroylated Shh peptide is necessary and sufficient for Disp-mediated transfer to HDL.
source: The cholesteroylated Shh peptide is necessary and sufficient for Disp-mediated transfer because artificially cholesteroylated mCherry associates with HDL in a Disp-dependent manner, whereas an N-palmitoylated Shh variant lacking C-cholesterol does not.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing mCherry-cholesterol association with HDL and lack of association for N-palmitoylated variants.

claim: Artificially cholesteroylated mCherry associates with HDL in a Disp-dependent manner.
source: The cholesteroylated Shh peptide is necessary and sufficient for Disp-mediated transfer because artificially cholesteroylated mCherry associates with HDL in a Disp-dependent manner, whereas an N-palmitoylated Shh variant lacking C-cholesterol does not.
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study.

claim: An N-palmitoylated Shh variant lacking C-cholesterol does not associate with HDL in a Disp-dependent manner.
source: The cholesteroylated Shh peptide is necessary and sufficient for Disp-mediated transfer because artificially cholesteroylated mCherry associates with HDL in a Disp-dependent manner, whereas an N-palmitoylated Shh variant lacking C-cholesterol does not.
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study.

claim: Disp-mediated Shh transfer to HDL is completed by proteolytic processing of the palmitoylated N-terminal membrane anchor.
source: Disp-mediated Shh transfer to HDL is completed by proteolytic processing of the palmitoylated N-terminal membrane anchor.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study supported by experimental data.

claim: Dual-processed soluble Shh has moderate bioactivity.
source: In contrast to dual-processed soluble Shh with moderate bioactivity, HDL-associated N-processed Shh is highly bioactive.
evidence: This is experimental data from bioactivity assays in the current study.

claim: HDL-associated N-processed Shh is highly bioactive.
source: In contrast to dual-processed soluble Shh with moderate bioactivity, HDL-associated N-processed Shh is highly bioactive.
evidence: This is experimental data from bioactivity assays in the current study.

claim: The purpose of generating different soluble forms of Shh from the dual-lipidated precursor is to tune cellular responses in a tissue-type and time-specific manner.
source: We propose that the purpose of generating different soluble forms of Shh from the dual-lipidated precursor is to tune cellular responses in a tissue-type and time-specific manner.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Hedgehog (Hh) ligands activate an evolutionarily conserved signaling pathway that provides instructional cues during tissue morphogenesis.
source: Hedgehog (Hh) ligands activate an evolutionarily conserved signaling pathway that provides instructional cues during tissue morphogenesis and, when misregulated, contributes to developmental disorders and cancer.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Hh signaling.

claim: Misregulated Hh signaling contributes to developmental disorders and cancer.
source: Hedgehog (Hh) ligands activate an evolutionarily conserved signaling pathway that provides instructional cues during tissue morphogenesis and, when misregulated, contributes to developmental disorders and cancer.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Hh signaling.

claim: Hhs require autocatalytic covalent cholesteroylation of the C-terminus.
source: Hhs are unique in that they require autocatalytic covalent cholesteroylation of the C-terminus (Porter et al., 1996b) and N-terminal palmitoylation by a separate Hh acyltransferase (Hhat) activity (Pepinsky et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Hhs require N-terminal palmitoylation by a separate Hh acyltransferase (Hhat) activity.
source: Hhs are unique in that they require autocatalytic covalent cholesteroylation of the C-terminus (Porter et al., 1996b) and N-terminal palmitoylation by a separate Hh acyltransferase (Hhat) activity (Pepinsky et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Both lipids tightly bind Hh to the plasma membrane of producing cells to effectively prevent unregulated ligand release.
source: Both lipids tightly bind Hh to the plasma membrane of producing cells to effectively prevent unregulated ligand release (Peters et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a cited reference.

claim: Signaling to distant target cells requires the regulated solubilization of Hh from the membrane of ligand-producing cells.
source: Signaling to distant target cells therefore requires the regulated solubilization of Hh from the membrane of ligand-producing cells, a process that is facilitated by vertebrate and invertebrate Dispatched (Disp) orthologs in vitro (Ehring et al., 2022) and in vivo (Burke et al., 1999; Ma et al., 2002; Kawakami et al., 2002; Nakano et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple cited references.

claim: Vertebrate and invertebrate Dispatched (Disp) orthologs facilitate Hh solubilization in vitro.
source: Signaling to distant target cells therefore requires the regulated solubilization of Hh from the membrane of ligand-producing cells, a process that is facilitated by vertebrate and invertebrate Dispatched (Disp) orthologs in vitro (Ehring et al., 2022) and in vivo (Burke et al., 1999; Ma et al., 2002; Kawakami et al., 2002; Nakano et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by cited references including the authors' previous work.

claim: Vertebrate and invertebrate Dispatched (Disp) orthologs facilitate Hh solubilization in vivo.
source: Signaling to distant target cells therefore requires the regulated solubilization of Hh from the membrane of ligand-producing cells, a process that is facilitated by vertebrate and invertebrate Dispatched (Disp) orthologs in vitro (Ehring et al., 2022) and in vivo (Burke et al., 1999; Ma et al., 2002; Kawakami et al., 2002; Nakano et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited references.

claim: Disp contains 12 transmembrane helices and 2 extracellular domains.
source: Disp contains 12 transmembrane helices and 2 extracellular domains and belongs to the resistance-nodulation-division family of transmembrane efflux pumps.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about Disp.

claim: Disp belongs to the resistance-nodulation-division family of transmembrane efflux pumps.
source: Disp contains 12 transmembrane helices and 2 extracellular domains and belongs to the resistance-nodulation-division family of transmembrane efflux pumps.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Disp classification.

claim: Resistance-nodulation-division family pumps normally maintain cellular homeostasis and remove toxic compounds.
source: Normally, such pumps maintain cellular homeostasis and remove toxic compounds.
evidence: This is general knowledge about the function of resistance-nodulation-division family pumps.

claim: Disp contains a conserved multi-pass transmembrane domain known as the sterol sensing domain (SSD).
source: In addition, Disp contains a conserved multi-pass transmembrane domain known as the sterol sensing domain (SSD), which regulates the homeostasis of free or esterified cellular cholesterol in other SSD proteins (Hall et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about Disp supported by a cited reference.

claim: The sterol sensing domain (SSD) regulates the homeostasis of free or esterified cellular cholesterol in other SSD proteins.
source: In addition, Disp contains a conserved multi-pass transmembrane domain known as the sterol sensing domain (SSD), which regulates the homeostasis of free or esterified cellular cholesterol in other SSD proteins (Hall et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SSD function supported by a cited reference.

claim: Disp's molecular architecture is consistent with Disp extraction of free cholesterol from the plasma membrane to remove it from the cell.
source: This molecular architecture is consistent with Disp extraction of free cholesterol from the plasma membrane to remove it from the cell (Ehring et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural features and supported by the authors' previous work.

claim: It has been suggested that Disp extracts the C-terminally linked Hh sterol to solubilize Hh in the extracellular compartment.
source: In addition, given its established role in Hh release, it has been suggested that Disp also extracts the C-terminally linked Hh sterol to solubilize Hh in the extracellular compartment (Tukachinsky et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from the literature supported by a cited reference.

claim: Disp activity alone is not sufficient to solubilize the vertebrate Hh family member Sonic hedgehog (Shh) from the plasma membrane.
source: However, Disp activity alone is not sufficient to solubilize the vertebrate Hh family member Sonic hedgehog (Shh) from the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study and previous work.

claim: A second synergistic factor required for maximal Shh signaling is the soluble extracellular glycoprotein Scube2.
source: A second synergistic factor required for maximal Shh signaling is the soluble extracellular glycoprotein Scube2 (Signal sequence, cubulin [CUB] domain, epidermal growth factor [EGF]-like protein 2) (Hall et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a cited reference.

claim: Disp-mediated extraction of dual-lipidated Shh from the plasma membrane delivers it to Scube2.
source: One way to explain the Disp/Scube2 synergy is that Disp-mediated extraction of dual-lipidated Shh from the plasma membrane delivers it to Scube2, a mechanism that depends on the C-terminal cysteine-rich and CUB domains of Scube2 (Tukachinsky et al., 2012; Creanga et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from the literature supported by cited references.

claim: The Disp-to-Scube2 delivery mechanism depends on the C-terminal cysteine-rich and CUB domains of Scube2.
source: One way to explain the Disp/Scube2 synergy is that Disp-mediated extraction of dual-lipidated Shh from the plasma membrane delivers it to Scube2, a mechanism that depends on the C-terminal cysteine-rich and CUB domains of Scube2 (Tukachinsky et al., 2012; Creanga et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from the literature supported by cited references.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation of Disp and Scube2 with Shh provides in vitro support for the Disp-to-Scube2 delivery mechanism.
source: In vitro support for this mechanism comes from co-immunoprecipitation of Disp and Scube2 with Shh (Tukachinsky et al., 2012; Creanga et al., 2012) and from structural data (Wierbowski et al., 2020).
evidence: This is experimental evidence from the literature supported by cited references.

claim: Structural data provide in vitro support for the Disp-to-Scube2 delivery mechanism.
source: In vitro support for this mechanism comes from co-immunoprecipitation of Disp and Scube2 with Shh (Tukachinsky et al., 2012; Creanga et al., 2012) and from structural data (Wierbowski et al., 2020).
evidence: This is structural evidence from the literature supported by a cited reference.

claim: Lipoprotein particles (LPPs) are proposed carriers for Disp-extracted lipidated Hh/Shh.
source: Other proposed carriers for Disp-extracted lipidated Hh/Shh include lipoprotein particles (LPPs) (Eugster et al., 2007; Palm et al., 2013; Panáková et al., 2005), exosomes as carriers of internalized and re-secreted Hhs (Gradilla et al., 2014; Vyas et al., 2014; Matusek et al., 2014), and micellous Hh assemblies (Zeng et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from the literature supported by cited references.

claim: Exosomes are proposed carriers of internalized and re-secreted Hhs.
source: Other proposed carriers for Disp-extracted lipidated Hh/Shh include lipoprotein particles (LPPs) (Eugster et al., 2007; Palm et al., 2013; Panáková et al., 2005), exosomes as carriers of internalized and re-secreted Hhs (Gradilla et al., 2014; Vyas et al., 2014; Matusek et al., 2014), and micellous Hh assemblies (Zeng et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from the literature supported by cited references.

claim: Micellous Hh assemblies are proposed carriers for Disp-extracted lipidated Hh/Shh.
source: Other proposed carriers for Disp-extracted lipidated Hh/Shh include lipoprotein particles (LPPs) (Eugster et al., 2007; Palm et al., 2013; Panáková et al., 2005), exosomes as carriers of internalized and re-secreted Hhs (Gradilla et al., 2014; Vyas et al., 2014; Matusek et al., 2014), and micellous Hh assemblies (Zeng et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from the literature supported by a cited reference.

claim: Another proposed mode of Shh release is Disp-regulated proteolytic processing (termed shedding) from the plasma membrane.
source: Another proposed mode of Shh release is Disp-regulated proteolytic processing (termed shedding) from the plasma membrane (Ehring et al., 2022) by two major plasma membrane-associated sheddases, A Disintegrin and Metalloproteinase (ADAM) 10 and 17 (Dierker et al., 2009; Ohlig et al., 2011; Damhofer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from the literature supported by cited references.

claim: Two major plasma membrane-associated sheddases are A Disintegrin and Metalloproteinase (ADAM) 10 and 17.
source: Another proposed mode of Shh release is Disp-regulated proteolytic processing (termed shedding) from the plasma membrane (Ehring et al., 2022) by two major plasma membrane-associated sheddases, A Disintegrin and Metalloproteinase (ADAM) 10 and 17 (Dierker et al., 2009; Ohlig et al., 2011; Damhofer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: The role of Scube2 in the shedding model is to enhance proteolytic processing of both terminal lipidated Shh peptides in a CUB domain-dependent manner.
source: The role of Scube2 in the shedding model is to enhance proteolytic processing of both terminal lipidated Shh peptides in a CUB domain-dependent manner (Jakobs et al., 2014; Jakobs et al., 2016; Jakobs et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from the literature supported by cited references.

claim: CUB function in regulated shedding of other substrates often involves substrate recognition and induced structural changes in the substrate to increase turnover.
source: Consistent with this, CUB function in regulated shedding of other substrates often involves substrate recognition and induced structural changes in the substrate to increase turnover (Bourhis et al., 2013; Jakobs et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge about CUB domain function supported by cited references.

claim: Disp and Scube2 synergistically enhance Shh shedding into the cell culture medium.
source: First, we confirmed by SDS-PAGE/immunoblotting and reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) that Disp and Scube2 synergistically enhance Shh shedding into the cell culture medium (Jakobs et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding confirmed in the current study and supported by a cited reference.

claim: Repeated washing of Disp- and Shh-expressing cells to remove all traces of serum abolished Shh release.
source: We also found that repeated washing of Disp- and Shh-expressing cells to remove all traces of serum abolished Shh release, and that high levels of serum promoted the solubilization of a previously unknown, highly bioactive Shh variant that lacks its palmitoylated N-terminus but retains its cholesteroylated C-terminus.
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study.

claim: High levels of serum promoted the solubilization of a previously unknown, highly bioactive Shh variant that lacks its palmitoylated N-terminus but retains its cholesteroylated C-terminus.
source: We also found that repeated washing of Disp- and Shh-expressing cells to remove all traces of serum abolished Shh release, and that high levels of serum promoted the solubilization of a previously unknown, highly bioactive Shh variant that lacks its palmitoylated N-terminus but retains its cholesteroylated C-terminus.
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study.

claim: Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) analyses revealed co-elution of the novel Shh variant with serum apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1).
source: Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) analyses revealed co-elution of this novel Shh variant with serum apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), the major protein component of the serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL) fraction.
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study.

claim: ApoA1 is the major protein component of the serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL) fraction.
source: Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) analyses revealed co-elution of this novel Shh variant with serum apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), the major protein component of the serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL) fraction.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HDL composition.

claim: Purified HDL restored solubilization of the N-processed, bioactive Shh variant from washed cells.
source: Consistent with this observation, purified HDL restored solubilization of the N-processed, bioactive Shh variant from washed cells.
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study.

claim: Palmitoylated N-terminal Shh membrane anchors are not transferred by Disp, but undergo shedding to complete Shh transfer to HDL.
source: In contrast, palmitoylated N-terminal Shh membrane anchors are not transferred by Disp, but undergo shedding to complete Shh transfer to HDL.
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study.

claim: The results unify previously disparate models of Disp-, sheddase-, and LPP-mediated Shh solubilization into a comprehensive system.
source: These results unify previously disparate models of Disp-, sheddase-, and LPP-mediated Shh solubilization into a comprehensive system that is fully consistent with published reports on in vivo Disp functions (Burke et al., 1999; Ma et al., 2002; Callejo et al., 2011; Kawakami et al., 2002; Nakano et al., 2004), in vivo Scube2 functions (Hollway et al., 2006; Johnson et al., 2012; Kawakami et al., 2005), the in vitro role of the Scube2 CUB domain (Jakobs et al., 2017; Jakobs et al., 2014), the Disp structure (Chen et al., 2020; Li et al., 2021), and required N-terminal – but not C-terminal – shedding during in vivo Hh solubilization (Kastl et al., 2018; Schürmann et al., 2018; Manikowski et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings supported by multiple cited references.

claim: The results are consistent with the established importance of Hh C-cholesterol for Hh association into 'large punctate' structures visible by light microscopy that may represent Hh-LPP complexes.
source: The results are also consistent with the established importance of Hh C-cholesterol for Hh association into 'large punctate' structures visible by light microscopy that may represent Hh-LPP complexes (Gallet et al., 2003; Gallet and Therond, 2005; Gallet et al., 2006), C-cholesterol-dependent Hh spreading (Li et al., 2006; Tukachinsky et al., 2012), and previously established in vivo roles of LPPs in Hh biofunction (Eugster et al., 2007; Panáková et al., 2005; Palm et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings supported by cited references.

claim: The results are consistent with C-cholesterol-dependent Hh spreading.
source: The results are also consistent with the established importance of Hh C-cholesterol for Hh association into 'large punctate' structures visible by light microscopy that may represent Hh-LPP complexes (Gallet et al., 2003; Gallet and Therond, 2005; Gallet et al., 2006), C-cholesterol-dependent Hh spreading (Li et al., 2006; Tukachinsky et al., 2012), and previously established in vivo roles of LPPs in Hh biofunction (Eugster et al., 2007; Panáková et al., 2005; Palm et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings supported by cited references.

claim: The results are consistent with previously established in vivo roles of LPPs in Hh biofunction.
source: The results are also consistent with the established importance of Hh C-cholesterol for Hh association into 'large punctate' structures visible by light microscopy that may represent Hh-LPP complexes (Gallet et al., 2003; Gallet and Therond, 2005; Gallet et al., 2006), C-cholesterol-dependent Hh spreading (Li et al., 2006; Tukachinsky et al., 2012), and previously established in vivo roles of LPPs in Hh biofunction (Eugster et al., 2007; Panáková et al., 2005; Palm et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings supported by cited references.

claim: The Disp-produced, HDL-bound, mono-lipidated Shh variant helps to meet the requirements for regulating Hh activity in specific cell types and developing tissues.
source: We propose that the Disp-produced, HDL-bound, mono-lipidated Shh variant presented in this work helps to meet the requirements for regulating Hh activity in specific cell types and developing tissues.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Scube2 enhances Shh solubilization from nt ctrl cells.
source: This confirmed that Scube2 enhances Shh solubilization from nt ctrl cells (Figure 1A, arrowhead; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A includes all transfection and loading controls) and that Shh solubilization from Disp-/- cells is always strongly impaired (Figure 1A'; Ehring et al., 2022; Tukachinsky et al., 2012; Creanga et al., 2012).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Shh solubilization from Disp-/- cells is always strongly impaired.
source: This confirmed that Scube2 enhances Shh solubilization from nt ctrl cells (Figure 1A, arrowhead; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A includes all transfection and loading controls) and that Shh solubilization from Disp-/- cells is always strongly impaired (Figure 1A'; Ehring et al., 2022; Tukachinsky et al., 2012; Creanga et al., 2012).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figure 1A' and supported by cited references.

claim: The electrophoretic mobility of most Shh released from nt ctrl cells was increased over that of the corresponding dual-lipidated cellular precursor.
source: We also confirmed that the electrophoretic mobility of most Shh released from nt ctrl cells (Figure 1A, arrowhead) was increased over that of the corresponding dual-lipidated cellular precursor (Figure 1A, asterisk; Jakobs et al., 2014; Jakobs et al., 2016; Ehring et al., 2022).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figure 1A and supported by cited references.

claim: RP-HPLC demonstrated that the observed increase in electrophoretic mobility was caused by the proteolytic removal of both lipidated terminal peptides from the cellular protein.
source: RP-HPLC of the solubilized material shown in Figure 1A (arrowhead) demonstrated that the observed increase in electrophoretic mobility was caused by the proteolytic removal of both lipidated terminal peptides from the cellular protein (Figure 1A'', this post-translational modification of Shh is referred to as shedding throughout this article; see Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–G for cellular dual-lipidated or artificially produced monolipidated and unlipidated Shh standard proteins and see Ehring et al., 2022, which rules out alternative modes of Shh deacylation).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figure 1A'' and supported by a cited reference.

claim: Transgenic Disp expression in Disp-/- cells restored Shh shedding and solubilization, confirming the specificity of the assay.
source: Transgenic Disp expression in Disp-/- cells restored Shh shedding and solubilization, confirming the specificity of the assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 2H; Ehring et al., 2022).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2H and supported by a cited reference.

claim: Coexpression of the cholesterol pump Patched (Ptch1) achieved the same phenotypic reversal as transgenic Disp expression in Disp-/- cells.
source: Strikingly, the same phenotypic reversal was achieved by the coexpression of the cholesterol pump Patched (Ptch1) (Zhang et al., 2018), which depletes the plasma membrane of free sterols (Figure 1—figure supplement 2H; Ehring et al., 2022).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2H and supported by cited references.

claim: Ptch1 depletes the plasma membrane of free sterols.
source: Strikingly, the same phenotypic reversal was achieved by the coexpression of the cholesterol pump Patched (Ptch1) (Zhang et al., 2018), which depletes the plasma membrane of free sterols (Figure 1—figure supplement 2H; Ehring et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Plasma membrane cholesterol has an indirect 'second messenger' role in the regulation of Smoothened downstream of Ptch1 in Shh receiving cells.
source: This suggests an indirect 'second messenger' role of plasma membrane cholesterol not only in the regulation of Smoothened downstream of Ptch1 in Shh receiving cells (Zhang et al., 2018; Kinnebrew et al., 2019; Kinnebrew et al., 2022), but also in the regulation of Shh release by Disp in producing cells (Ehring et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and supported by cited references.

claim: Plasma membrane cholesterol has an indirect 'second messenger' role in the regulation of Shh release by Disp in producing cells.
source: This suggests an indirect 'second messenger' role of plasma membrane cholesterol not only in the regulation of Smoothened downstream of Ptch1 in Shh receiving cells (Zhang et al., 2018; Kinnebrew et al., 2019; Kinnebrew et al., 2022), but also in the regulation of Shh release by Disp in producing cells (Ehring et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and supported by a cited reference.

claim: Scube2 and Disp synergistically and specifically increased Shh release via shedding from the cell surface.
source: Taken together, Scube2 and Disp synergistically and specifically increased Shh release via shedding from the cell surface (as indicated by the appearance of 'lower'-sized bands compared to those of cellular proteins, Figure 1A, and the decreased hydrophobicity of solubilized Shh, Figure 1A'').
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1A''.

claim: The prohormone convertase furin cleaves Disp at a conserved processing site to activate it and to release Shh from the cell surface.
source: It was recently shown that the prohormone convertase furin cleaves Disp at a conserved processing site to activate it and to release Shh from the cell surface (Stewart et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a cited reference.

claim: CMK reduced Shh shedding from the cell surface in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: Indeed, CMK reduced Shh shedding from the cell surface in a concentration-dependent manner (Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figure 2A–C.

claim: Repeated careful prior washing of cells to quantitatively remove all traces of serum severely impaired Disp- and Scube2-mediated Shh solubilization into serum-free media.
source: During these assays, we also found that repeated careful prior washing of cells to quantitatively remove all traces of serum severely impaired Disp- and Scube2-mediated Shh solubilization into serum-free media (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: The minimal requirements of Na+-driven, Disp-mediated Shh extraction and hand-over to Scube2 are not sufficient to release Shh.
source: The first is that the minimal requirements of Na+-driven, Disp-mediated Shh extraction and hand-over to Scube2 (Wang et al., 2021) are not sufficient to release Shh.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and a cited reference.

claim: Shh self-assembly by the law of mass action is not supported because this process should solubilize Shh regardless of the presence or absence of serum.
source: The second is that Shh self-assembly by the law of mass action (Koleva et al., 2015) is also not supported because this process should solubilize Shh regardless of the presence or absence of serum.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and a cited reference.

claim: One function of Disp is to extract free plasma membrane cholesterol and transfer it to a soluble sink for removal from the cell.
source: In contrast, we previously found that one function of Disp is to extract free plasma membrane cholesterol and transfer it to a soluble sink for removal from the cell (Ehring et al., 2022; Ehring and Grobe, 2021).
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work supported by cited references.

claim: In vertebrates, HDLs represent a soluble sink for 'free' peripheral cholesterol.
source: In vertebrates, HDLs represent a soluble sink for 'free' peripheral cholesterol (Luo et al., 2020), and HDLs and the pharmacological cholesterol chelator methyl-β-cyclodextrin have previously been shown to increase Shh shedding (Ehring et al., 2022; Jakobs et al., 2014; Ohlig et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a cited reference.

claim: HDLs and the pharmacological cholesterol chelator methyl-β-cyclodextrin have previously been shown to increase Shh shedding.
source: In vertebrates, HDLs represent a soluble sink for 'free' peripheral cholesterol (Luo et al., 2020), and HDLs and the pharmacological cholesterol chelator methyl-β-cyclodextrin have previously been shown to increase Shh shedding (Ehring et al., 2022; Jakobs et al., 2014; Ohlig et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: The permissive factor missing from the shedding assay is most likely a soluble cholesterol acceptor, such as HDL or a related serum LPP.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the permissive factor missing from our shedding assay is most likely a soluble cholesterol acceptor, such as HDL or a related serum LPP, as previously reported (Palm et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and supported by a cited reference.

claim: Increased serum concentrations during Shh solubilization did not appear to much affect Disp- and Scube2-specific Shh shedding.
source: Increased serum concentrations during Shh solubilization (0.05% FCS [Figure 3B, quantified in Figure 3B'], 5% FCS [Figure 3C, quantified in Figure 3C'], and 10% FCS [Figure 3D, quantified in Figure 3D']) did not appear to much affect Disp- and Scube2-specific Shh shedding (arrowheads, Figure 3E in contrast shows unregulated release of unprocessed Shh [the 'top' band] in the presence of 10% FCS).
evidence: This is experimental data from the current study shown in Figures 3B-D.
